problem:
An inner product on $V={R}^{3}$ is defined as $⟨x,y⟩=2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{3}{y}_{3}.$ 
Calculate the norm of the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ under this inner product.
worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $v$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖=\sqrt{⟨v,v⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $‖v‖$ using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖ & =\sqrt{⟨v,v⟩} \\  & =\sqrt{2\cdot (1\cdot 1)+3\cdot ((-2)\cdot (-2))+2\cdot ((-1)\cdot (-1))} \\  & =\sqrt{2+12+2} \\  & =\sqrt{16} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
